official_alerts.headline: Freeze Warning issued November 25 at 12:27AM CST until November 25 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Fort Worth TX
official_alerts.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 27.

* WHERE...Portions of North and Central Texas.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM CST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
official_alerts.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and
unfrozen water.

Protect the 4 Ps from cold temperatures: People, pets, pipes, plants.

official_alerts.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 25 at 12:51AM CST until November 26 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Paducah KY
official_alerts.description:
Our first winter storm of the season is set to impact portions of
our region as we head into the Thanksgiving holiday. A sharp gradient
between very little snow and impactful snow amounts is expected. That
sharp cutoff appears likely to setup within 25 miles of the
Mississippi River, with latest trends shifting further west with the
heavier axis.

* WHAT...Wet snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 1 to 2 inches
with the highest totals potentially approaching 3 inches near the
Mississippi River.

* WHERE...Alexander, Jackson, Perry IL, and Union Counties in
southern Illinois.

* WHEN...From 3 PM this afternoon to noon CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning
commutes.
official_alerts.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
can be obtained by visiting www.weather.gov/pah/roads

official_alerts.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 25 at 2:55AM EST until November 27 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
official_alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday
night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
official_alerts.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
official_alerts.area: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

official_alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 24 at 3:32PM EST until November 26 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
official_alerts.description:
A disturbance will pass near or south of the local area Wednesday.
Saturated soils from recent heavy rainfall will increase the risk of
additional flooding across portions of central Florida. Rainfall
amounts of 1 to 2 inches are forecast with localized higher totals of
3 to 4 inches possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including, Indian River,
Martin, Saint Lucie, Brevard, and Okeechobee counties.

* WHEN...From 1 AM EST Wednesday through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are forecast with localized
higher amounts of 3 to 4 inches will be possible. Heavy rainfall
over saturated soils may lead to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
official_alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

official_alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 3:01AM EST until November 26 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
official_alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee,
Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 PM this evening
to 5 AM EST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from late
tonight through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
official_alerts.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWS wind: 42.6 km/h (forecast-period peak) during 2026-11-26 13:00 UTC to 2026-11-26 14:00 UTC, with intervals covering the window. official_alerts.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 25 at 1:48AM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
official_alerts.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 55 mph
expected.

* WHERE...District of Columbia, central, north central, northeast,
northern, southern, and western Maryland, northern and northwest
Virginia, and eastern and panhandle West Virginia.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 4 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The combination of a soaking rain and very
windy conditions could result in many downed trees.
official_alerts.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

official_alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 3:01AM EST until November 26 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
official_alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee,
Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 PM this evening
to 5 AM EST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from late
tonight through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
official_alerts.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

risk_policy.hko_policy: HKO code/type and original text are not converted into invented CAP severity. risk_policy.missing_data: LOW is a lower-bound screening result, not confirmation of safety; unknown hazards cannot lower a known grade.
risk_policy.dwd_altitude_policy: DWD warnings with issuer altitude bounds are retained as geographically/time-matched advisories; without requested site elevation they do not raise the screening index. Original issuer severity and instructions are not downgraded or rewritten.
risk_policy.provider_selection: Full-window NWS values are preferred for US canonical numeric fields; MET values remain visible. GFS precipitation uses only explicit non-overlapping six-hour source bounds and can recover incomplete canonical rainfall coverage; nested cumulative intervals are excluded. Lower independent rainfall cannot erase a known higher hazard grade. MET instant sustained wind, MET timestamped gust values and GFS gust samples do not fill missing interval coverage. MET JSON does not supply gust period bounds; its precipitation intervals are not gust validity intervals. MET thunder evidence uses each full issued interval; an overlapping interval is not a localized event time.
risk_policy.precipitation_method: Non-overlapping source intervals; boundary fractions are time-proportional estimates, not observed hourly rainfall.

official_alerts.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 55 mph
expected.

* WHERE...District of Columbia, central, north central, northeast,
northern, southern, and western Maryland, northern and northwest
Virginia, and eastern and panhandle West Virginia.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 4 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The combination of a soaking rain and very
windy conditions could result in many downed trees.

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

risk_policy.hko_policy: HKO code/type and original text are not converted into invented CAP severity. risk_policy.missing_data: LOW is a lower-bound screening result, not confirmation of safety; unknown hazards cannot lower a known grade.
risk_policy.dwd_altitude_policy: DWD warnings with issuer altitude bounds are retained as geographically/time-matched advisories; without requested site elevation they do not raise the screening index. Original issuer severity and instructions are not downgraded or rewritten.
risk_policy.provider_selection: Full-window NWS values are preferred for US canonical numeric fields; MET values remain visible. The screening grade is the maximum known hazard grade across all fetched independent forecasts (including discrete GFS and NDFD gust samples; NDFD is an alternative NWS delivery) and applicable official alerts, not an averaged forecast or calibrated probability. GFS precipitation uses only explicit non-overlapping six-hour source bounds and can recover incomplete canonical rainfall coverage; nested cumulative intervals are excluded. Lower independent rainfall cannot erase a known higher hazard grade. MET instant sustained wind, MET timestamped gust values and GFS gust samples do not fill missing interval coverage. MET JSON does not supply gust period bounds; its precipitation intervals are not gust validity intervals. MET thunder evidence uses each full issued interval; an overlapping interval is not a localized event time.
